nodes.label: Portable folder publication
nodes.rationale: Defines clean self-contained win-x64 Release publication and required host executable/native SQLite payload verification without archive packaging.

nodes.label: RC MSIX packaging stance
nodes.rationale: Defines RC-only Dobby MSIX identity, SDK tool discovery, manifest-verified staging, Installed mode rewrite, and dormant MSI fallback.

nodes.label: CycloneDX dependency evidence
nodes.rationale: Generates CycloneDX SBOM, dependency inventory, and vulnerability result; it fails for stale/missing assets, audit failure, or vulnerabilities while license review remains owner-gated.

nodes.label: Portable support artifact
nodes.rationale: Produces a versioned self-contained artifact with manifest/hash inventory, Production trust profile, PortableSupport metadata, and an isolated support data root.

nodes.label: Isolated portable launch verification
nodes.rationale: Launches an exact portable build against a fresh temporary root, verifies interactive login and clean exit, and never targets a customer profile.

nodes.label: Security regression test slices
nodes.rationale: Runs unit and integration ownership slices for trust, parsing, licensing, recovery, authentication throttling, protected storage, and persistence fault boundaries.

nodes.label: Observable credential-warmup completion
nodes.rationale: Changes warmup to return its exact completion Task while the login UI explicitly fire-and-forgets it and tests await it deterministically.

nodes.label: Flake-sensitive verification matrix
nodes.rationale: Runs repeated focused, full integration, and sequential project matrices with persisted logs, while distinguishing a non-reproduction result from proof of no flakes.

nodes.label: Release candidate evidence runner
nodes.rationale: Collects hashed repository-owned verification evidence and only considers GA inputs when schema-validated external evidence satisfies each exact gate.

nodes.label: Test-only recovery trust fixture
nodes.rationale: Contains a PEM-encoded public key explicitly marked TEST-ONLY for recovery integration fixtures.

nodes.label: Owner recovery response CLI
nodes.rationale: Wraps the Admin CLI for recovery-response generation from a request, device public key, signing profile, and output path.

nodes.label: Dev/QA plugin package signing CLI
nodes.rationale: Wraps the Admin CLI for sample package signing with input, signing profile, output, and optional trust/report/overwrite options.

nodes.label: Non-executing plugin package verification
nodes.rationale: Validates bytes, manifest/content rules, and signature without loading code; it returns safe typed rejection data in its report.

nodes.label: Trusted in-process plugin posture
nodes.rationale: Separates public purpose-specific trust keys, prohibits private keys in the workspace/process/logs, and rejects loading code not fully trusted for in-process execution.

nodes.label: Detached plugin license creation CLI
nodes.rationale: Wraps the Admin CLI and requires package, signing, customer/deployment, device binding, validity, revision, and output inputs.

nodes.label: Plugin page rendering and fault UI
nodes.norm_label: plugin page rendering and fault ui
nodes.rationale: Defines approved plugin page rendering, background operation status propagation, exception-boundary use, and safe persisted fault presentation.

nodes.label: ReadOnlyExpired runtime-mode enforcement
nodes.rationale: Requires a Security-owned single customer/deployment context, lookup-only licensing, and host-owned typed gates at concrete mutation surfaces.

nodes.label: Plugins Manager lifecycle orchestration
nodes.rationale: Defines host-owned UI flow for local package install, durable list/detail state, enable/disable/uninstall, audit, confirmation, and safe feedback.

nodes.label: Deterministic Credential Warmup Completion Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: deterministic credential warmup completion implementation plan

nodes.label: Flake-sensitive wait triage classification
nodes.rationale: Each observed test wait is classified as a legitimate dispatcher pump, explicit completion, deterministic clock advance, or a timing risk requiring reproduction before behavior changes.

nodes.label: Deterministic flake-prevention guardrails
nodes.rationale: The plan requires current-failure reproduction, wait classification, repeat-verification artifacts, and precise language rather than speculative WPF production fixes.

nodes.label: Observable credential warmup task
nodes.rationale: ILoginCredentialWarmupWorkflow exposes an awaitable warmup completion task so tests replace polling with explicit TaskCompletionSource synchronization.

nodes.label: CRM shell visual language
nodes.rationale: Sets a light, compact CRM presentation with icon rail, tab chrome, polished work panel, pipeline content, and theme-owned visual tokens.

nodes.label: Workstation tab lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Defines ordered tab state, active-tab navigation, Home replacement for closing the sole tab, and deterministic adjacent-tab activation.

nodes.label: Chrome-scale tabs with native captions
nodes.rationale: Requires compact shrinking tabs with internal close actions, one trailing new-tab button, and native Windows caption controls.

nodes.label: Owner and managed-user model
nodes.rationale: The first local account becomes Owner; later users are managed local users constrained by permissions.

nodes.label: Owner recovery flow
nodes.rationale: Owner password recovery uses exported request and imported response files.

nodes.label: Plugin packaging and licensing scope
nodes.rationale: Defines signed .dobbyplugin installation, Plugins > License import, and non-disclosing plugin runtime modes.

nodes.label: Three-bar shell navigation
nodes.rationale: Defines TopToolbar, Sidebar, Third Bar, main content, and status/progress shell composition.

nodes.label: Dobby.Contracts boundary
nodes.rationale: Holds plugin-visible contracts, extension, event, storage, capability-policy, and ordering contracts without runtime implementation.

nodes.label: Dobby.PluginFramework
nodes.rationale: Owns discovery, packaging, compatibility, DI bridge, load context, deferred activation, and dependency resolution.

nodes.label: Dobby.Security boundary
nodes.rationale: Owns authentication, authorization, trust, and host-controlled capability boundaries.

nodes.label: Phase 1 technology stack selection

nodes.rationale: Uses narrow capability-oriented contracts, security-owned enforcement, asynchronous decisions, and non-disclosing denial behavior.

nodes.label: Stable UI ordering model
nodes.rationale: Establishes Group, Weight, stable tiebreaking, and bounded user overrides for composed UI entries.

nodes.label: Plugin DI registration boundary
nodes.rationale: Defines IPluginModule registration, activation context, plugin lifetimes, disposal, and capability-limited host services.

nodes.label: Per-plugin AssemblyLoadContext strategy
nodes.rationale: Uses an isolated non-collectible AssemblyLoadContext per plugin, host-pinned shared dependencies, and plugin-local dependencies.

nodes.label: Post-login deferred plugin activation
nodes.rationale: Forbids fresh scanning and code execution before login, then uses a post-login activation cycle with per-plugin failure isolation.

nodes.label: Deterministic plugin dependency graph
nodes.rationale: Requires stable topological, sequential post-login activation with visible skipped states for missing, invalid, circular, or failed dependencies.

nodes.label: Plugin communication policy
nodes.rationale: Permits Contracts interfaces, public integration events, and declared extension points while prohibiting direct plugin/runtime references and storage backdoors.

nodes.label: P95 reference hardware release gate
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: A defined median hardware baseline, 100-run P95 methodology, and 20% regression budget make startup thresholds reproducible.

nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.norm_label: az-az default culture and missing-key fallback
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 UI defaults to az-AZ, uses resources for visible strings, and records production missing keys as diagnostics rather than audit events.

nodes.label: Namespaced localization resource ownership
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: Host resources use project/feature/category/key names under Dobby.Localization, while plugin resources remain inside plugin assemblies.

nodes.label: Canonical signed plugin package boundary
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: A signed .dobbyplugin manifest and deterministic file hashes are separate from a detached vendor-signed .dobbylicense artifact.

nodes.label: Canonical UI and code terminology glossary
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.norm_label: canonical ui and code terminology glossary
nodes.rationale: Stable technical terms remain in code while visible UI terminology is supplied through localization resources and the canonical mapping.

nodes.label: Registry-based operation permissions
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: A host-owned registry uses closed canonical verbs and typed OperationPermissionCapability evaluation; unknown targets or verbs fail closed.

nodes.label: Hierarchical navigation contribution descriptors
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: TopToolbar, Sidebar, and Third Bar render parent/child contribution levels while retaining a closed manifest target vocabulary.

nodes.label: Process-lifetime in-memory work sessions
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: Live built-in or plugin work screens can be explicitly minimized and restored in memory, without Phase 1 restart recovery.

nodes.label: Bound license lifecycle state machine v2
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.norm_label: bound license lifecycle state machine v2
nodes.rationale: v2 defines signed detached license binding, persisted lifecycle states, read-only expiry behavior, and plugin-visible runtime modes; it is superseded by ADR-0060.

nodes.label: Single active customer/deployment context
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: Each Phase 1 installation maintains one host-internal customerId/deploymentId context that license import validates without exposing it to plugins.

nodes.label: Non-disclosing plugin runtime modes
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: ICapabilityLicensing returns FullAccess, ReadOnlyExpired, or Denied while host boundaries remain authoritative for enforcement.

nodes.label: SQLite full-DB encryption provider direction
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: Option A requires a SQLite3MultipleCiphers or SQLCipher-compatible full-database encryption layer and retains unprotected DB artifacts as release blockers.

nodes.label: DPAPI scope mapping and key wrapping
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.norm_label: dpapi scope mapping and key wrapping
nodes.rationale: Machine-bound materials use LocalMachine plus application entropy and ACLs, while per-Windows-user remembered/session data uses CurrentUser.

nodes.label: Mode-bounded storage providers
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: Standalone uses local encrypted SQLite while Branch Shared uses LAN PostgreSQL authority plus DeviceLocal protected profiles, with implementation tiering kept explicit.

nodes.label: Branch Shared authentication boundary
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: Branch Shared credentials and permissions stay authoritative in PostgreSQL; unavailable authority fails closed and BranchSetup is separate from host runtime.

nodes.label: Durable credential throttling and cryptographic recovery
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.norm_label: durable credential throttling and cryptographic recovery
nodes.rationale: Remembered login retains only username metadata; durable throttling, atomic password changes, and signed key-pair-based Owner recovery replace replayable passwords and fuzzy hardware binding.

nodes.label: Trusted in-process plugin and declarative UI v2
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.norm_label: trusted in-process plugin and declarative ui v2
nodes.rationale: Approved vendor-signed in-process plugins are not sandboxed; bounded package validation, separate signing key purposes, and declarative host-rendered UI establish the v2 contract.

nodes.label: Last-known-good atomic license import
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: v3 licenses sign granted/revoked intent, derive runtime states, retain the last-known-good state for bad candidates, and atomically commit valid imports with attestation and audit.

nodes.label: Strict pre-auth runtime and atomic mutation boundary
nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.norm_label: strict pre-auth runtime and atomic mutation boundary
nodes.rationale: An executable pre-auth allow-list and event ledger constrain construction as well as calls; authoritative mutations require one transaction or durable outbox.

nodes.community_name: ADR-0046: UI and Code Terminology Mapping
nodes.rationale: The guide defines ADR lifecycle, required structure, cross-reference and update rules, and says controlling 2026-08 ADRs override conflicting older wording.

nodes.label: Standalone completion plan
nodes.rationale: An ordered, test-first plan brings Standalone Dobby to release readiness while holding Branch Shared outside implementation scope until explicitly reopened.

nodes.label: Executable findings register
nodes.rationale: A 25-finding and 69-row register distinguishes executed behavior evidence from weaker or deferred classifications and maps each finding to closure work and tests.

nodes.label: Identity hardening workstream
nodes.rationale: The workstream freezes credential contracts, removes replayable passwords, makes throttle durable, enforces login-first scopes, makes mutations atomic, and replaces fuzzy recovery authorization.

nodes.label: Provider-owned mutation transaction and outbox
nodes.rationale: Multi-write security workflows bind repositories, audit, and idempotent outbox records to one provider transaction, with post-commit delivery and deterministic fault injection.

nodes.label: Trusted plugin platform hardening
nodes.rationale: The plan defines reviewed trusted in-process plugins, streaming bounded packages, purpose-separated crypto, crash-consistent installation, async lifecycle, declarative UI, and accurate runtime fault attribution.

nodes.label: Derived license lifecycle and runtime gates
nodes.norm_label: derived license lifecycle and runtime gates
nodes.rationale: License v3 signs only Granted or Revoked intent; bounded trusted inputs derive lifecycle state, valid imports atomically update LKG state, and command-bound policy gates all existing runtime surfaces.

nodes.label: Behavior-first WPF shell completion
nodes.rationale: Shell state is lifetime-owned and orchestration is extracted from code-behind; heavyweight work is cancellable off-dispatcher and accessibility/localization behavior is proven by deterministic WPF tests.

nodes.label: Reproducible release evidence
nodes.rationale: Signed artifacts, portable support builds, installed MSIX upgrade proof, supply-chain inputs, and a per-candidate hashed evidence manifest are required; GA remains blocked without external production inputs and installed evidence.

nodes.label: Branch Shared reopening gates
nodes.rationale: Branch Shared requires explicit owner decisions, accepted threat-model contracts, a separately approved Tier A skeleton, and later Tier B operational evidence before any customer runtime claim.

nodes.label: License v3 lifecycle truth table
nodes.rationale: Top-down evaluation derives Denied, Pending, Active, Grace, or ReadOnlyExpired from signed intent, validation, trusted time, and checked UTC boundaries rather than accepting an artifact status.

nodes.label: P1 scripted operator path
nodes.rationale: Vendor-side Admin services expose fixed CLI wrappers for package signing, license creation, recovery response, and independent package verification with safe output, canonical profiles, and stable exit codes.
nodes.source_location: P1 Minimal Scripted Operator Path; Approved P1 CLI contract

nodes.label: Structured redacted audit and diagnostics
nodes.rationale: Audit events are typed accountable records and technical diagnostics are local support data; both enforce safe fields and redaction, while host support export remains available across all license lifecycle states.
nodes.source_location: Audit Event Taxonomy; Diagnostics; 2026-08 Hardening Amendment

nodes.label: Verified local backup and restore
nodes.rationale: Authenticated host maintenance creates encrypted SQLite online snapshots and restores only verified staged candidates with immutable audit/outbox overlays, quarantine, rollback, and safe startup recovery.

nodes.label: Standalone retention floors
nodes.rationale: Authenticated background maintenance preserves a 365-day audit floor, protects audit referenced by pending outbox entries, and applies snapshot cleanup only after safe promotion.

nodes.label: Design-system tokens and asset boundary
nodes.rationale: Host, Admin, and plugin visuals use shared typography, spacing, motion, reduced-motion, semantic theme, and asset rules while plugin assets remain host-validated and plugin UI avoids Dobby.UI dependencies.

nodes.label: Branch Shared device lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Future Branch Shared registration issues server-side device identities and support-safe metadata; recovery uses a protected device asymmetric key rather than raw hardware or fuzzy matching.
nodes.source_location: Device Identity Boundary; Registration; 2026-08 Device Identity Amendment

nodes.label: Atomic non-disclosing license import
nodes.rationale: Permission-gated import validates a license against fixed host context and package bindings; malformed or invalid candidates preserve LKG, while valid v3 grants atomically commit state, attestation, audit, and outbox evidence.

nodes.label: BranchSetup provisioning boundary
nodes.rationale: A separate customer-side BranchSetup context owns setup credentials, schema creation, first Owner provisioning, device registration, and purpose-signed setup authorization without granting those powers to Host or Admin.
nodes.source_location: Setup Context through Setup Evidence Routing; 2026-08 Provisioning Amendment

nodes.label: Plugin lifecycle and UI boundary
nodes.rationale: Plugins Manager safely installs, manages, and presents reviewed signed plugins through permission-gated, post-login, bounded, non-disclosing host-controlled flows with fault isolation.
nodes.source_location: P1 Scope; Local File Install; Runtime and Main Content Hosting; 2026-08 Hardening Amendment

nodes.label: Branch Shared PostgreSQL operational readiness
nodes.rationale: Tier B Branch Shared release requires a selected PostgreSQL runbook, isolated setup/runtime roles, grants and TLS checks, post-restore validation, credential rotation, and executed operational evidence.

nodes.label: Specs ownership index
nodes.rationale: The index defines each specification's canonical boundary and prevents duplicate schema or ownership authorities while directing completion status to the master execution plan.

nodes.label: Host-owned background operation contract
nodes.rationale: Long-running work reports host-controlled operation snapshots, progress, cancellation, correlation, and typed redacted failure information through Contracts.

nodes.label: Deterministic shell composition rendering
nodes.rationale: Shell rendering applies the established group, weight, and stable-tiebreak ordering model directly across canonical host-controlled surfaces.

nodes.label: Audit classification vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Names Implemented, Implemented-Weak, Partial, Incorrect, Unimplemented, Deferred-by-design, and Evidence-only classifications.

nodes.label: Document authority order
nodes.rationale: Establishes precedence among feature specifications, canonical documents, and implementation plans.

nodes.label: Dark blue-gray icon background
nodes.rationale: The lettermark is placed on a uniform dark blue-gray square field.

nodes.label: D lettermark
nodes.rationale: The image visibly presents a single uppercase D as the central mark.

nodes.label: Graphify workflow
nodes.rationale: Defines graph-first exploration and graph update after code changes.

nodes.label: SDK convenience surface
nodes.rationale: Dobby.SDK provides ergonomic helpers for stable Contracts without exposing host implementation, new capabilities, backing stores, raw licensing, WPF types, or service location.

nodes.label: Stable route identity and login-gated routing
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.norm_label: stable route identity and login-gated routing
nodes.rationale: Routes use stable invariant string keys, plugin routes are host-normalized, and unresolved or unauthorized routes fall back to Home.

nodes.label: Local structured diagnostics logging
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: Technical logs are local structured diagnostics with mandatory write-time redaction and no default telemetry or remote log shipping.

nodes.label: Append-only audit versus diagnostics boundary
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: Audit is an append-only public API record of accountable actions, while diagnostics is local technical troubleshooting data with separately governed export and retention.

nodes.label: Vendor-side admin and host boundary
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: Dobby.Admin is a separate vendor-side executable that reuses host application logic and uniquely handles customer records and signing flows, including Owner recovery artifacts.

nodes.label: Historical license lifecycle
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: This superseded ADR documents a historical signed offline license state machine and explicitly states that ADR-0051 and ADR-0053 own the current canonical lifecycle and plugin runtime surface.

nodes.label: Validated configuration and security floors
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: Dobby.Configuration owns ordered configuration sources and typed validation; configuration cannot weaken security, storage protection, trust verification, telemetry, or audit-redaction floors.

nodes.label: Correlation context ownership
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: Dobby.Core owns generation and async-flow context access; scopes preserve existing identifiers, explicitly propagate background work, and clear context on completion.

nodes.label: Plugin storage compartments
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: Internal host persistence is separated from explicit SharedDomainStorage and UserScopedStorage plugin compartments, with protected local data-at-rest and additional secret-field protection.

nodes.label: No-refresh session lifecycle
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: A single active authenticated session expires by absolute or idle timeout, explicit invalidation, or tamper detection; it is cleared rather than refreshed and returns the user to login.

nodes.label: Offline plugin signature verification
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: Plugin installation and activation fail closed after manifest, file-hash, ECDSA P-256 signature, and known-vendor verification using a build-embedded master public key.

nodes.label: Vendor master signing key ownership
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: A single vendor ECDSA P-256 private key remains offline on the vendor side; its public key is embedded at host build time and key rotation is deferred.

nodes.label: Historical tenant/customer scope
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: This superseded ADR records the earlier single-default-tenant primitive and states that ADR-0052 owns the current customer/deployment context model.

nodes.label: Typed declarative plugin manifest schema
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: The canonical camelCase manifest and JSON Schema constrain identity, integrity, capability, operation-target, extension, route, and file declarations with host-defined closed vocabularies.

nodes.label: Device-bound local password authentication
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: Core authentication is offline local password authentication with protected credentials, constrained remember-me behavior, explicit KDF floors, app-wide throttle, and atomic first-Owner bootstrap.

nodes.label: Historical device-bound Owner recovery
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: This superseded ADR specifies a historical file-based, vendor-signed, 24-hour, single-use Owner recovery response verified against a fuzzy five-source device fingerprint and consumed nonce.

nodes.label: Internal host adapter boundary
nodes.community_name: ADR-0039: Owner Password Recovery via Vendor-Signed Device-Bound Artefakt
nodes.rationale: Dobby.Infrastructure is an internal-only primitive and backing-adapter layer for hardware identity, protected storage, and persistence, wired by the host without a plugin-visible surface.

nodes.norm_label: task 02 execution note: plugin storage, runtime layout, audit boundary, and persistence maintenance

nodes.norm_label: task 03 execution note: login-first, auth policy, lock, password change, instrumentation, and work-session lifecycle

nodes.norm_label: task 04 execution note: rendered settings, user management, about, theme sync, and localization

nodes.label: Dev/QA sample plugin verification anchor
nodes.rationale: The sample is a non-production signed artifact that verifies manifest, hosting, permissions, results, faults, progress, and work-session paths.

nodes.label: Single-session lifecycle and cleanup boundary
nodes.rationale: Login establishes a single active session; logout disposes session-scoped services and work sessions, while lock preserves the session and in-memory work.

nodes.label: Permission-gated Settings and support-safe About
nodes.rationale: Settings exposes a fixed P1 category tree, gates User Management, shares theme/session preferences, and keeps About support-safe and license-import-free.

nodes.label: Host-owned shared import/export mapping
nodes.rationale: Future P2 mapping profiles are keyed by authenticated plugin identity, profile key, and field-model version while hosts own picker, mapping UI, transaction, and export boundaries.

nodes.label: Host-owned hierarchical and accessible shell
nodes.rationale: The WPF shell renders TopToolbar, Sidebar, Third Bar, main content, status, and minimized work strip through a host-owned, localized, token-based navigation model.

nodes.label: Protected storage taxonomy and bootstrap boundary
nodes.norm_label: protected storage taxonomy and bootstrap boundary
nodes.rationale: Encrypted host persistence separates host, shared-domain, and user-scoped plugin data; a closed pre-login table set and provider-neutral materialization pass preserve login-first limits.

nodes.label: Protected Owner and grant-only user operations
nodes.norm_label: protected owner and grant-only user operations
nodes.rationale: Owner is a protected all-grants principal; managed users are default-deny, service validation is mandatory, and first-user bootstrap atomically seeds user, permission state, and audit.

nodes.label: Explicit in-memory minimize and restore
nodes.rationale: Work screens are process-lifetime state, require explicit minimize or controlled close choices, and are never automatically restored after restart.

nodes.label: Portable folder publish contract
nodes.rationale: A PowerShell command publishes a self-contained win-x64 Dobby.Host folder and an architecture test prevents drift into zip packaging.

nodes.label: Chrome-like workspace tab state
nodes.rationale: ShellViewModel-owned tabs always open Home, retain route/title per tab, use deterministic close rules, and preserve existing work-session navigation authority.

nodes.label: CRM shell presentation polish
nodes.rationale: The approved design adds vector iconography, soft continuous shell surfaces, a dashboard/pipeline home panel, and a central soft-cutout secondary navigation area without changing workstation behavior.

nodes.label: Native caption controls and Chrome-scale tabs
nodes.norm_label: native caption controls and chrome-scale tabs
nodes.rationale: Titlebar rendering uses native Windows caption controls and bounded tab-width converters while retaining one trailing new-tab button and system close confirmation.

nodes.label: P1 release evidence gate closure
nodes.rationale: Release review remains blocked until production recovery evidence, compliant N=100 performance baseline evidence, MSIX execution evidence, leak scans, and final no-restore verification pass.

nodes.label: Dependency-ordered remaining product-work closure
nodes.rationale: The master plan sequences storage/auth, shared UI, plugin/license, sample/Admin, and installer evidence work with task-specific red tests and execution notes.

nodes.label: Authority reconciliation execution guardrail
nodes.rationale: Task 1 records a bounded source-authority and unsupported-KDF review surface, preserving prior dirty work and disallowing unapproved Argon2 expansion.

nodes.label: Plugin storage and runtime-layout execution boundary
nodes.norm_label: plugin storage and runtime-layout execution boundary
nodes.rationale: Task 2 explicitly protects Task 1 KDF wiring while adding post-login plugin storage, append-only migrations, logical folders, and support-safe persistence maintenance.

nodes.label: Login-first auth and lock lifecycle execution
nodes.norm_label: login-first auth and lock lifecycle execution
nodes.rationale: Task 3 scopes login-first enforcement, simple credential policy, LockViewModel, self-service password change, and controlled work-session lifecycle without starting shared UI redesign.

nodes.label: Settings source and localization execution lane
nodes.norm_label: settings source and localization execution lane
nodes.rationale: Task 4 deliberately confines work to settings models, localization, and preference seams until Task 5 owns shared WPF shell files.

nodes.label: Shared shell implementation lane
nodes.rationale: Task 5 takes sequential ownership of shell route activation, named WPF regions, profile actions, status feedback, minimized-strip rendering, and diagnostics export.
